title: Rocky
why: Apollo Creed stages his Bicentennial title fight on New Year's Day, 1 January 1976 — the date the whole film counts down to.
alt: The Poseidon Adventure (1972) — capsizes at midnight, the entire escape happens on 1 Jan; Platoon (1968 New Year's Day battle); Trading Places

title: The Beatles: Get Back
why: Opens on a title card reading Thursday 2 January 1969 — day one of the Twickenham sessions. Every subsequent day is date-stamped on screen.
alt: 1492: Conquest of Paradise (surrender of Granada, 2 Jan 1492)

title: The Turin Horse
why: Béla Tarr opens by narrating Nietzsche's collapse in Turin on 3 January 1889, throwing his arms around a flogged cab horse — then follows that horse.

title: Cromwell
why: Dramatises Charles I marching into the Commons to arrest the Five Members on 4 January 1642 — 'I see the birds have flown' — the spark for the Civil War.

title: An Officer and a Spy
why: Opens with the public degradation of Alfred Dreyfus in the courtyard of the École Militaire, 5 January 1895.
alt: The Time Machine (1960) — the second dinner party, 5 January 1900

title: Spotlight
why: The film climaxes on the Boston Globe's publication date: 6 January 2002, the morning the Spotlight team's first abuse story ran.
alt: Twelfth Night (1996) — the Feast of Epiphany; Blood Diamond (RUF assault on Freetown, 6 Jan 1999)

title: Galileo
why: Joseph Losey's Brecht adaptation turns on Galileo sighting the moons of Jupiter through his telescope on the night of 7 January 1610.

title: The Buccaneer
why: Jean Lafitte and Andrew Jackson at the Battle of New Orleans, fought 8 January 1815 — the film's entire climax.

title: Nicholas and Alexandra
why: Stages Bloody Sunday, 9 January 1905, when the Imperial Guard fired on Gapon's petitioners outside the Winter Palace.
alt: Battleship Potemkin (1925) — the 1905 revolution it triggered

title: Amelia
why: Earhart's solo Honolulu–Oakland flight, begun 11 January 1935 — the first by anyone, in either direction.

title: Walk the Line
why: The film is framed by Johnny Cash's concert at Folsom State Prison on 13 January 1968 — it opens and closes there.

title: Sully
why: US Airways 1549 ditches in the Hudson at 15:31 on 15 January 2009. The film replays that afternoon repeatedly.
alt: Selma (Martin Luther King Jr born 15 January 1929)

title: Jarhead
why: Swofford's war begins with the opening of the Desert Storm air campaign on the night of 16/17 January 1991.

title: Scott of the Antarctic
why: Scott's party reaches the South Pole on 17 January 1912 to find Amundsen's tent already there — the film's devastating centrepiece.

title: The Raven
why: A Poe murder mystery, released to mark the poet's birthday: Edgar Allan Poe born 19 January 1809.

title: Nixon
why: Built around the presidency that begins and ends on Inauguration Day — Nixon sworn in 20 January 1969, and again 20 January 1973.

title: Zulu
why: The defence of Rorke's Drift, which began on the afternoon of 22 January 1879 and ran through the night.
alt: Zulu Dawn (1979) — Isandlwana, the same morning; Victoria & Abdul (Victoria died 22 Jan 1901)

title: Steve Jobs
why: Act one is the Macintosh launch at Flint Center, 24 January 1984 — played out in real time backstage.

title: The Square
why: Opens in Tahrir Square on 25 January 2011, the first day of the Egyptian revolution, and follows the occupation from there.

title: Australia Day
why: Three interlocking stories that all unfold over the twelve hours of Australia Day, 26 January.

title: Amadeus
why: Mozart was born on 27 January 1756; the film is his life told as Salieri's confession.
alt: 27 January is Holocaust Memorial Day — the liberation of Auschwitz, 1945

title: Argo
why: The six houseguests fly out of Mehrabad on Swissair 363 on the morning of 28 January 1980 — the escape the whole film builds to.

title: Bloody Sunday
why: Greengrass covers a single day almost hour by hour: the Derry civil rights march of 30 January 1972.
alt: Gandhi (1982) — opens with the assassination, 30 January 1948; Full Metal Jacket (Tet, 30 Jan 1968)

title: Lincoln
why: The whole film drives at one roll-call: the House passing the Thirteenth Amendment on 31 January 1865.
